subject: Aurum Health RFP - PHI handling, data residency & deployment options
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@aurumhealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: David Park <david.park@aurumhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Aurum RFP - PHI handling, residency questions

Hi Karthik —

Thanks for the fast turnaround after our demo last week. Attached is the formal RFP (Aurum_RFP_20261201.pdf) and a short list of clarifying questions from our security & procurement teams. High level asks we need answered to advance to vendor short-list:

- Can Redwood commit to PHI processing exclusively within our hosted region (US-east) for Aurum's tenants?
- Does Redwood offer a private/VPC-only deployment for our workloads, and what data egress controls are possible?
- We need details on key management: customer-managed keys (KMS) + HSM options and whether keys can be colocated in our cloud account.
- Audit/logging retention: default retention and support for 7+ year export for legal hold.
- Are there standard interfaces for batch PHI ingest (SFTP) and AR/ETL workflows that avoid storing unencrypted payloads at rest?

Please review the RFP and share a mutual action plan & timeline if Redwood is interested. We’re aiming to get short-list decisions by Dec 15.

Thanks — happy to hop on a call if easier.

Samantha Lee
Sr. Vendor Ops Manager
Aurum Health

Attachments: Aurum_RFP_20261201.pdf
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@aurumhealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 09:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Aurum RFP - PHI handling, residency questions

Samantha —

Appreciate the clear RFP and timeline. Redwood is very interested; we believe we can meet the bulk of Aurum’s security and residency constraints. I’ve attached a draft Mutual Action Plan (Redwood_Mutual_Action_Plan_20261202.xlsx) with proposed milestones: short-list response (this week), security deep-dive (week of Dec 6), contract redline (Dec 10–12), and optional on-prem/air-gapped PoC the week of Dec 20.

To your specific questions up front:
1) Region-bound processing: yes — we support pinning customer workloads to a region (US-east) in our Hosted environment. For added assurance we can provide per-tenant routing policies and region-only enforcement logs.
2) Private/VPC-only deployment: we offer Redwood Private (VPC or on-prem). For cloud VPC mode, control plane connectivity can be limited by customer-managed private endpoints; compute and PHI processing remain in your VPC or our dedicated private subnet depending on the model chosen. See the attached diagram (redwood-deploy-options-diagram.png).
3) Key management: we support customer-managed KMS with HSM-backed keys. Keys may be hosted in the customer cloud account (bring-your-own-key) or managed via Redwood HSM appliances for private deployments; see kms-hsm-architecture.pdf for options and latency characteristics.
4) Audit/logging retention: default audit retention is 90 days. We offer extended retention add-ons and an export capability to push logs to your S3/archive for legal hold (we can support 7+ year retention on exported archives).
5) SFTP & batch ingestion: we provide an SFTP gateway option that streams files directly into transient processing pipelines and encrypts at-rest by default. For customers that require zero-at-rest persistence for raw payloads, we can implement a streaming-only ingestion path with immediate KV-cache transformation and ephemeral storage.

Next steps I propose:
- Technical deep-dive: Wed Dec 8, 10am ET (30–45m) with Monica (security engineering) and Vivek (infrastructure) to walk architecture and telemetry.
- Contracting: we can share a HIPAA-ready BAA and an initial commercial redline by Dec 9.

If that timeline works, I’ll send calendar invites and the deep-dive agenda.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_Mutual_Action_Plan_20261202.xlsx; redwood-deploy-options-diagram.png; kms-hsm-architecture.pdf
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@aurumhealth.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 14:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Aurum RFP - PHI handling, residency questions

Samantha / Karthik —

Adding some technical clarifications ahead of the deep-dive so Aurum’s infra and security teams can triage quickly:

- Network isolation: for VPC deployments we support private endpoints and no public egress from compute nodes. Customers can require NAT gateway restrictions or VPC peering that prevents any traffic leaving the designated region.
- Dataflow for batch SFTP: we recommend an ingestion pattern where files land in a customer-controlled S3 bucket, trigger an event to a transient processing instance in the same region, and the instance writes only tokenized results to persistent stores. Raw files are encrypted server-side with your CMK and lifecycle rules set to immediate transition to Glacier or deletion after processing if desired.
- KMS semantics: if you bring your own key, Redwood never has the unwrap capability. All encryption/decryption calls are proxied through your KMS in your account. For on-prem/HSM appliances, keys remain in the hardware and remote unwrap is restricted to attested hosts.
- Audit & telemetry: we produce structured audit events (JSON) for access, model invocation, and admin actions. We can stream these to your SIEM (Splunk/Datadog) or to an S3 bucket in your account. Retention policy is configurable per-customer; we can support regulatory holds by exporting to immutable storage.
- Contract/security docs: we will supply a SOC 2 Type II report, penetration test summary, and our HIPAA BAA draft. Note that some evidence (internal change logs) will require an NDA/audit agreement; we can coordinate a limited-scope evidence package.

Edge cases & tradeoffs to note:
- Latency: the private VPC model with customer-hosted KMS adds ~10–30ms to token operations depending on KMS location; for very low-latency clinical use-cases we recommend colocated HSMs or an in-region KMS in the same cloud account.
- Cost: dedicated pools and long-term log export add to committed spend; we’ll itemize estimates once we know expected token volume.

I’ll be on the Dec 8 deep-dive with architecture diagrams and a short demo of the SFTP-to-tokenization flow.

Cheers,
Monica Patel
Security & Reliability Lead — Redwood Inference

Karthik / Monica —

Thanks — that allay many of our concerns and gives procurement what they need to move Redwood to the short-list. Confirming next steps on our side:

- We’ll circulate your MAP internally and provide a redline window by Dec 10.
- Security team will join the Dec 8 deep-dive (David Park and two infra engineers). Please send the calendar invite and the meeting agenda.
- We’d like an initial cost estimate for the VPC-private model with bring-your-own-key (monthly committed baseline + egress/export costs).

Also please include a sample HIPAA BAA draft and the SOC2 Type II cover page in the docs you share ahead of the call. If PoC is necessary we may start with a cloud VPC deployment before evaluating on-prem.

Samantha
